items.stem: What does a displayed formula show?
options: Every atom and every bond in the molecule
The simplest whole-number ratio of atoms
Only the number of each type of atom
items.answer: Every atom and every bond in the molecule
items.markingKey: Displayed formula: all atoms and all covalent bonds drawn.

items.stem: Explain the difference between a molecular formula and a structural formula, using ethanol as the example.
items.answer: Molecular C₂H₆O shows only numbers of atoms; structural CH₃CH₂OH shows how the atoms are grouped/arranged.

items.stem: Explain why the general formula of an alkene is CₙH₂ₙ while that of an alkane is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
items.answer: The C=C double bond uses two bonding electrons per carbon that would otherwise bond to hydrogen, so an alkene has two fewer H atoms.

items.stem: State the molecular formula of pentane and calculate its relative molecular mass.
items.answer: C₅H₁₂; 72

items.stem: For butane, CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃: (a) write the molecular formula, (b) write the empirical formula, (c) calculate the relative molecular mass.
items.answer: (a) C₄H₁₀ (b) C₂H₅ (c) 58

items.stem: A hydrocarbon contains, by mass, C 85.7%, H 14.3%. Its relative molecular mass is 84. Calculate its empirical formula and deduce its molecular formula.
items.answer: Empirical CH₂; molecular C₆H₁₂
items.markingKey: divide each % by Ar [1]; divide by smallest to get ratio [1]; empirical CH₂ (Mr 14) [1]; 84/14 = 6 so C₆H₁₂ [1]

items.stem: An organic compound X has the structural formula CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH. (a) Name the homologous series and the functional group. (b) Calculate the percentage by mass of carbon.
items.answer: (a) carboxylic acid; –COOH (carboxyl) (b) 54.5%

items.stem: A bottle in a sixth-form practical class is labelled "ethene, CH₂=CH₂". (a) State the general formula of this homologous series. (b) Calculate the percentage by mass of carbon. (c) Name the next member of the same homologous series and give its formula.
items.answer: (a) CₙH₂ₙ (b) 85.7% (c) propene, C₃H₆

items.stem: What is the general formula of the alkanes?
items.answer: CₙH₂ₙ₊₂

items.stem: Which is the structural formula of ethanol?
items.answer: CH₃CH₂OH
items.markingKey: Structural formula shows the arrangement of atoms group by group.

items.stem: Explain why one carbon atom in a displayed formula always has four bonds drawn.
items.answer: Carbon has four outer electrons and forms four covalent bonds.

items.stem: Explain why two different compounds can have the same empirical formula, giving an example.
items.answer: The empirical formula is only the simplest ratio; e.g. ethene C₂H₄ and propene C₃H₆ are both CH₂.

items.stem: A compound contains C 83.7%, H 16.3% by mass. Calculate its empirical formula.
items.answer: C₃H₇
items.markingKey: % ÷ Ar for each element [1]; simplest ratio [1]; formula [1]

items.stem: State the molecular formula of hexane and calculate its relative molecular mass.
items.answer: C₆H₁₄; 86

items.stem: A hydrocarbon contains, by mass, C 82.8%, H 17.2%. Its relative molecular mass is 58. Calculate its empirical formula and deduce its molecular formula.
items.answer: Empirical C₂H₅; molecular C₄H₁₀
items.markingKey: divide each % by Ar [1]; divide by smallest to get ratio [1]; empirical C₂H₅ (Mr 29) [1]; 58/29 = 2 so C₄H₁₀ [1]

items.stem: An organic compound X has the structural formula CH₃CH₂CH₂COOH. (a) State the general formula of this homologous series. (b) Calculate the relative molecular mass. (c) Describe what the displayed formula would show.
items.answer: (a) CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH (b) 88 (c) Every atom and every covalent bond; each carbon with four bonds.

items.stem: An organic compound X has the structural formula CH₂=CH₂. (a) Calculate the relative molecular mass. (b) Calculate the percentage by mass of carbon. (c) Name the next member of the same homologous series and give its formula.
items.answer: (a) 28 (b) 85.7% (c) propene, C₃H₆

items.stem: What is the name of CH₃CH₂CH₃?
items.answer: propane

items.stem: Explain how the name "propan-1-ol" describes the structure of the molecule.
items.answer: prop- = 3 carbons; -an- = single C–C bonds; -1-ol = –OH group on the first carbon atom.

items.stem: Explain why there is no compound called "methene".
items.answer: An alkene needs a C=C double bond, which requires at least two carbon atoms.

items.stem: Give the structural formula of butane and identify its functional group and homologous series.
items.answer: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃; C–C single bonds only; alkane
items.markingKey: 1 mark formula; 1 mark functional group; 1 mark series [3]

items.stem: Give the structural formula of but-1-ene and identify its functional group and homologous series.
items.answer: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃; C=C double bond; alkene
items.markingKey: 1 mark formula; 1 mark functional group; 1 mark series [3]

items.stem: Four organic compounds are: A CH₃CH₂CH₃; B CH₄; C CH₂=CH₂; D CH₂=CHCH₃. (a) Which compounds are in the same homologous series, if any? (b) Which compound(s) would react with sodium carbonate to give carbon dioxide? (c) Give the functional group of compound A. (d) Give the molecular formula of compound B.
items.answer: (a) A and B (alkanes); C and D (alkenes) (b) none (c) C–C single bonds only (d) CH₄

items.stem: Which prefix shows a chain of four carbon atoms?
items.answer: but-

items.stem: Explain why ethanoic acid and ethanol have similar names but different properties.
items.answer: Both have two carbons (eth-) but different functional groups (–COOH and –OH), which determine their chemical properties.

items.stem: A student names CH₃COOCH₂CH₃ as "ethyl methanoate". Explain the error and give the correct name.
items.answer: The acid part CH₃COO– has two carbons (ethanoate) and the alcohol part –CH₂CH₃ is ethyl: ethyl ethanoate.

items.stem: What is the name of the ester formed from methanol and propanoic acid?
items.answer: methyl propanoate

items.stem: Name, and give the structural formula of, the ester made from methanol and ethanoic acid.
items.answer: methyl ethanoate; CH₃COOCH₃

items.stem: Four organic compounds are: A HCOOH; B CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃; C CH₃OH; D CH₃CH₂COOH. (a) Which compounds are in the same homologous series, if any? (b) Which compound(s) would turn aqueous bromine from orange to colourless? (c) Which compound(s) would react with sodium carbonate to give carbon dioxide? (d) Give the molecular formula of compound B.
items.answer: (a) A and D (carboxylic acids) (b) none (c) A, D (d) C₄H₁₀

items.stem: Four organic compounds are: A HCOOH; B CH₂=CHCH₃; C CH₃CH₂CH₂OH; D CH₃CH₂COOH. (a) Which compounds are in the same homologous series, if any? (b) Which compound(s) would turn aqueous bromine from orange to colourless? (c) Which compound(s) would react with sodium carbonate to give carbon dioxide? (d) Give the functional group of compound A. (e) Give the molecular formula of compound B.
items.answer: (a) A and D (carboxylic acids) (b) B (c) A, D (d) –COOH (carboxyl) (e) C₃H₆

items.stem: Which statement describes members of a homologous series?
options: They have the same general formula and similar chemical properties
They have the same molecular formula
items.answer: They have the same general formula and similar chemical properties
items.markingKey: Homologous series: same functional group and general formula, similar chemical properties, trend in physical properties.

items.stem: Explain why the members of a homologous series have similar chemical properties.
items.answer: They have the same functional group, which determines how they react.

items.stem: Explain why the boiling points of alkanes increase as the number of carbon atoms increases.
items.answer: Larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces of attraction, so more energy is needed to separate them.

items.stem: Use the general formula of the alkenes to write the formula of the member with 7 carbon atoms and calculate its relative molecular mass.
items.answer: C₇H₁₄; Mr = 98

items.stem: Use the general formula of the alkenes to write the formula of the member with 20 carbon atoms and calculate its relative molecular mass.
items.answer: C₂₀H₄₀; Mr = 280

items.stem: A student plots the boiling points of the first five alcohols against the number of carbon atoms. Data: methanol 65 °C; ethanol 78 °C; propan-1-ol 97 °C; butan-1-ol 117 °C; pentan-1-ol 138 °C. (a) Which of these compounds are gases at 25 °C? (b) Give two other characteristics of a homologous series. (c) Write the molecular formula of hexan-1-ol.
items.answer: (a) none (b) Same functional group; similar chemical properties; differ by CH₂; same general formula. (c) C₆H₁₃OH

items.stem: Explain why methane is a gas but hexane is a liquid at room temperature.
items.answer: Hexane molecules are larger, with stronger intermolecular forces, so its boiling point (69 °C) is above room temperature; methane’s is −162 °C.

items.stem: Ethanol and propan-1-ol are in the same homologous series. Explain what this means.
items.answer: They have the same general formula (CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH), the same –OH functional group and similar chemical properties; they differ by CH₂.

items.stem: Deduce whether ethene, CH₂=CH₂, and propanoic acid, CH₃CH₂COOH, belong to the same homologous series. Explain your answer.
items.answer: No: ethene is an alkene (C=C double bond) but propanoic acid is a carboxylic acid (–COOH (carboxyl)).
items.markingKey: 1 mark conclusion; 1 mark functional group/general formula reasoning [2]

items.stem: The boiling points of some alcohols are: methanol 65 °C; ethanol 78 °C; propan-1-ol 97 °C; butan-1-ol 117 °C; pentan-1-ol 138 °C. Predict the boiling point of hexan-1-ol and explain the trend.
items.answer: About 157 °C (accept 148 to 173 °C); boiling point increases as the chain gets longer because intermolecular forces get stronger.
items.markingKey: 1 mark prediction in range; 1 mark trend explained [2]

items.stem: The boiling points of some alkanes are: methane −162 °C; ethane −89 °C; propane −42 °C; butane −1 °C; pentane 36 °C; hexane 69 °C. Predict the boiling point of heptane and explain the trend.
items.answer: About 98 °C (accept 79 to 104 °C); boiling point increases as the chain gets longer because intermolecular forces get stronger.
items.markingKey: 1 mark prediction in range; 1 mark trend explained [2]

items.stem: A student plots the boiling points of the first five alcohols against the number of carbon atoms. Data: methanol 65 °C; ethanol 78 °C; propan-1-ol 97 °C; butan-1-ol 117 °C; pentan-1-ol 138 °C. (a) State the general formula of the alcohols. (b) Describe the trend shown. (c) Explain the trend.
items.answer: (a) CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH (b) Boiling point increases as the number of carbon atoms increases. (c) Larger molecules have stronger intermolecular forces, needing more energy to separate.

items.stem: A student plots the boiling points of the first five alcohols against the number of carbon atoms. Data: methanol 65 °C; ethanol 78 °C; propan-1-ol 97 °C; butan-1-ol 117 °C; pentan-1-ol 138 °C. (a) Describe the trend shown. (b) Predict the boiling point of hexan-1-ol. (c) Which of these compounds are gases at 25 °C? (d) Give two other characteristics of a homologous series. (e) Write the molecular formula of hexan-1-ol.
items.answer: (a) Boiling point increases as the number of carbon atoms increases. (b) About 157 °C (c) none (d) Same functional group; similar chemical properties; differ by CH₂; same general formula. (e) C₆H₁₃OH

items.stem: What are structural isomers?
options: Compounds in the same homologous series
Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons
Compounds with the same structural formula but different molecular formulae
items.answer: Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae

items.stem: Explain why butane and methylpropane have different boiling points even though they have the same molecular formula.
items.answer: They have different structures; the branched methylpropane has a smaller surface contact between molecules, so weaker intermolecular forces and a lower boiling point.

items.stem: Explain why there are no isomers of propane.
items.answer: Three carbon atoms can only be joined in one way in a chain; any other drawing is the same molecule.

items.stem: Ethyl methanoate has the structural formula HCOOCH₂CH₃. Give the name and structural formula of one structural isomer of ethyl methanoate.
items.answer: propanoic acid: CH₃CH₂COOH; methyl ethanoate: CH₃COOCH₃ (any one)
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct structural formula; 1 mark name [2]

items.stem: Methyl methanoate has the structural formula HCOOCH₃. Give the name and structural formula of one structural isomer of methyl methanoate.
items.answer: ethanoic acid: CH₃COOH (any one)
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct structural formula; 1 mark name [2]

items.stem: A chemist in Auckland separates two liquids, both with molecular formula C₂H₄O₂, from a mixture. (a) Calculate the relative molecular mass of C₂H₄O₂. (b) State the total number of structural isomers with formula C₂H₄O₂ that are listed in the coursebook and name any not already given. (c) Suggest why the isomers can be separated by fractional distillation.
items.answer: (a) 60 (b) 2: ethanoic acid, methyl methanoate (c) Different structures give different boiling points.

items.stem: Which pair are structural isomers?
items.answer: butane and methylpropane

items.stem: Explain why ethanoic acid and methyl methanoate are isomers but belong to different homologous series.
items.answer: Both are C₂H₄O₂ (same molecular formula) but have different functional groups: –COOH (acid) and –COO– (ester).

items.stem: A student draws CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₃ and CH₂(CH₃)CH₂CH₃ and says they are isomers. Explain why the student is wrong.
items.answer: Both are the same straight chain of four carbons (butane); bending the chain does not change the structure.

items.stem: But-2-ene has the structural formula CH₃CH=CHCH₃. Give the name and structural formula of one structural isomer of but-2-ene.
items.answer: but-1-ene: CH₂=CHCH₂CH₃; methylpropene: CH₂=C(CH₃)CH₃ (any one)

items.answer: methylpropane: CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃ (any one)
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct structural formula; 1 mark name [2]

items.answer: (a) Compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulae. (b) CH₃CH(CH₃)CH₃

items.stem: Butan-2-ol has the structural formula CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃. Give the name and structural formula of one structural isomer of butan-2-ol.
items.answer: butan-1-ol: CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH; 2-methylpropan-1-ol: (CH₃)₂CHCH₂OH (any one)
items.markingKey: 1 mark correct structural formula; 1 mark name [2]

items.stem: Compounds P and Q both have the molecular formula C₄H₁₀O. P is CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH and Q is CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃. (a) Name the compound CH₃CH₂CH₂CH₂OH. (b) Give the structural formula of butan-2-ol. (c) State the total number of structural isomers with formula C₄H₁₀O that are listed in the coursebook and name any not already given.
items.answer: (a) butan-1-ol (b) CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃ (c) 3: butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol
